definition.description: Parses cron expressions and calculates upcoming run times. Supports standard 5-field cron syntax (minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week) as well as common presets. Returns the next N scheduled run times, a human-readable description of the schedule, and validation status. Useful for scheduling workflows, understanding cron schedules, and debugging timing issues in automated tasks.

inputFields.helpText: A standard 5-field cron expression in the format: MINUTE HOUR DAY MONTH WEEKDAY. Each field accepts: numbers (0-59 for minutes), ranges (1-5), lists (1,3,5), steps (*/15 for every 15), or wildcards (*). Also supports presets: @yearly, @monthly, @weekly, @daily, @hourly. Examples: '0 9 * * 1-5' runs at 9:00 AM on weekdays, '*/30 * * * *' runs every 30 minutes, '0 0 1 * *' runs at midnight on the 1st of each month.

How many upcoming run times to calculate and return. The parser will iterate through the schedule starting from the 'From Date' and collect this many future occurrences. Useful for previewing a schedule or validating that a cron expression produces the expected timing pattern. Maximum recommended: 100.

The starting point for calculating upcoming run times. If omitted, uses the current date and time. Accepts ISO 8601 format (2024-01-15T10:30:00Z) or common date formats. Useful for testing how a schedule will behave in the future or for historical analysis of what runs would have occurred.

outputParameters.description: The next scheduled run time in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2024-01-15T09:00:00.000Z). This is the first occurrence after the 'From Date'.
JSON array of the next N scheduled run times, where N is specified by the 'Number of Runs' input. Each time is in ISO 8601 format.
Human-readable description of the cron schedule, such as 'At minute 0 past hour 9 on Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri'. Useful for displaying to end users or for logging.
The normalized cron expression that was parsed. If a preset like @daily was used, this shows the expanded form (0 0 * * *).
True if the cron expression was successfully parsed and is syntactically correct. False if the expression has invalid syntax or unsupported features.
The actual number of run times that were calculated. May be less than requested if the schedule has limited occurrences within the search window.
True if the parsing operation failed due to invalid input or an unsupported cron syntax.
Detailed error message explaining why the parsing failed, such as 'Cron must have 5 fields' or 'Invalid minute value'.
